newsitem.title: UK: Edlund and Olsson score aces at Brtish Open. [CORRECTED 11:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Edlund and Olsson score aces at Brtish Open. [CORRECTED 11:42 GMT]

text.p: Swedes Dennis Edlund and Daniel Olsson shot holes-in-one in the second round of the British Open on Friday.
Edlund aced the 126-yard Postage Stamp eighth, the shortest hole on the British Open rota of courses, with a nine iron on a calm, sunny second morning of the tournament.
It is the hole famously aced in 1973 by 71-year-old American Gene Sarazen, who had won the Open in 1932. (Corrects dates and Sarazen's age.)
Edlund's great shot, however, will not help him to beat the halfway cut when it is made at the end of Friday's second round. He shot 87 in the first round on Thursday.
Olsson, an amateur, aced the 210-yard fifth with a five iron.
On Thursday, another Swede, Pierre Fulke, holed in one at the 179-yard 14th, just a week after he scored an ace in the opening round of the Loch Lomond World Invitational.
